title: refline
summary: Add a reference line y = m*x + b to the current or specified axes.

gpu_support.notes: `refline` creates a graphics object and does not perform numeric GPU computation.

description: `refline` appends straight reference lines to the current or specified axes and returns the created line handle or handles when requested. With no coefficients it adds least-squares lines for eligible scatter-style series in the axes. With coefficients it draws `y = m*x + b` over the current x-axis span.
behaviors: `refline()` and `refline(ax)` add least-squares reference lines for scatter-style series in the current or specified axes, matching MATLAB's `lsline`-style behavior.
`refline([m b])` and `refline(m,b)` draw a line with slope `m` and intercept `b`; coefficients must be finite numeric scalars.

The line uses explicit `XLim` when present. If x-limits are automatic, RunMat derives a finite x span from the target axes' visible data bounds and falls back to `[0,1]` only when no finite span is available.
As a RunMat extension, optional LineSpec and line Name/Value pairs such as `Color`, `LineStyle`, `LineWidth`, and `DisplayName` are accepted using the same parser as line plotting builtins.
The return value is a line graphics handle compatible with `get` and `set` for line properties such as `XData`, `YData`, `Color`, `LineStyle`, `LineWidth`, and `DisplayName`.

faqs.question: Does refline compute a least-squares fit?
faqs.answer: Yes, when called without explicit coefficients it adds least-squares lines for eligible scatter-style series in the axes. When coefficients are supplied, it draws exactly `y = m*x + b` and does not fit a model.
